rounds.text: Nexome Capital Markets Ltd trades at an exceptionally low valuation, sitting at a price-to-book ratio of 0.52x against a book value of ₹ 195 with the share price at ₹ 101 [E2], and commands a modest P/E ratio of 8.9 [E1] that significantly undercuts the sector benchmark P/E of 19.52x [E6]. This price disconnection from underlying value is underscored by a discounted cash flow intrinsic valuation of ₹ 419 per share, offering a substantial margin of safety of 75.9% [E45, E46], while a reverse DCF calculates that the current market price incorrectly prices in a -1.8% earnings contraction [E47]. Profit growth has been explosive, featuring a 5-year compound profit growth of 181% [E19] and a trailing twelve-month profit surge of 484% [E21], vastly outpacing a 5-year share price growth of just 19% [E23]. Furthermore, the company is almost debt-free [E59] with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.04x [E38], operates with robust short-term liquidity through a current ratio of 5.10x [E39], and benefits from a supportive Financial Services sector tailwind score of +1.00 [E75, E76]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over the last 5 years stands at -7% [E15] and the median return on equity over 5 years is constrained at 2% [E27].

Despite low headline multiples, Nexome Capital Markets Ltd exhibits severe top-line contraction and structural unprofitability in its core business operations, evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth of just 2% and a -15% decline over the trailing twelve months [E14, E17]. Operational volatility is extreme, highlighted by a quarterly operating margin plummeting to -61% in June 2026—a steep 70 percentage point drop from the year-ago quarter—while annual operating margin trends remain inconsistent [E31, E33]. The company's historical ability to generate returns for equity holders is exceptionally weak, reflected in a 10-year median ROE of a mere 2% and a low 3-year average ROE of 3% [E26, E28, E64]. Working capital health is deteriorating significantly, demonstrated by a surge in debtor days from 24.5 to 70.8 days and an increase in working capital days from 25.4 to 74.6 days [E65, E66]. Furthermore, institutional confidence is waning as foreign institutional holdings have dropped from 9.85% in September 2023 to 3.56% by June 2026, accompanied by a poor 12-month price return of -22.5% and a devastating historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -94.7% [E43, E52, E53]. Conceded: [E19] the company has delivered strong compounded profit growth of 181% over the last 5 years.

The bear focuses on top-line contraction through sales growth figures of 2% over 10 years and -15% over the trailing twelve months, yet glosses over the extraordinary compounding effect on the bottom line, where profits surged 181% over 5 years and 484% over the TTM [E14, E17, E19, E21]. Conceded: the company displays an inconsistent yearly operating margin trend and a negative quarterly margin in June 2026, but this overlooks the broader TTM operating margin expansion to 37% against 0% three years prior [E30, E31, E32]. While historical median ROE figures are low over multi-year periods, the company's recent operational efficiency shines through an ROA of 5.85% that comfortably outpaces the sector benchmark of 1.89% [E8, E26]. Although debtor and working capital days have increased, the firm remains conservatively financed with a negligible debt-to-equity ratio of 0.04x and a comfortable short-term current ratio of 5.10x [E38, E39, E65, E66]. The bear highlights waning foreign institutional holdings and historical drawdowns, but ignores that promoter confidence is actually rising with holdings increasing to 51.81% by June 2026, alongside an exceptionally low valuation offering a P/E of just 8.9x and a P/B of 0.52x against a supportive financial services sector tailwind [E1, E2, E42, E43, E53, E76].

Conceded: [E19, E21]. The bull cites bottom-line compounding, but ignores that top-line sales are contracting across every measured timeframe, including a 15% drop over the trailing twelve months and a negative 82% year-over-year quarterly plunge [E14, E15, E16, E17, E72]. While the bull points to a TTM operating margin expansion to 37%, it glosses over the severe collapse into negative territory at -61% for the June 2026 quarter and an inconsistent margin trend overall [E30, E31, E32, E33]. Conceded: [E8]. Although recent asset returns look favorable, the company's multi-year return on equity paints a chronically low picture with a 10-year median ROE of just 2% and a recent 3-year average flagged as poor at 3.13% [E26, E28, E64]. Furthermore, the bull minimizes rising operational friction, ignoring that debtor and working capital days have ballooned significantly alongside a recent spike in borrowings from Rs 3 Cr to Rs 7 Cr [E40, E65, E66]. Finally, while the bull highlights rising promoter ownership, it downplays the offsetting exodus of foreign institutional investors and extreme share price volatility featuring a historical maximum drawdown of nearly 95% [E42, E43, E53, E54].
